transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Solaris CTO), Alex Romero (Head of ML Ops), Priya Kaur (Security)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time—Samir here, AE at Redwood. We got about 45 minutes, we'll do a quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then the cost breakdown you asked about. Is that still the agenda on your end?

[00:22] Maya (Solaris): Yeah that sounds good. We really want to understand how costs map to our per-endpoint usage and whether Dedicated makes sense. Also Priya wants to ask a few security ones later.

[00:45] Samir: Perfect. I'll hand over to Lena for the demo part, she'll jump into the console and show the per-route views. Quick bit of context: we typically surface token-level cost and latency for each route, you can tag routes and get top-N breakdowns. Lena?

[01:10] Lena (Redwood): Cool thanks Samir. Hi all, logging into the Console now—bear with me, screen's a bit slow. Okay, dashboard home, this first card shows global usage: token counts, requests per minute, and a cost projection for the month. You can see we also have percentile latency lines so you can spot spikes. A note: the KV cache in the runtime shows up in the metrics, sometimes the exporter labels it as "KV cash" in older agents, ignore that if you see it.

[01:38] Alex (Solaris): Quick question—how real-time is the data? We need to alert on sudden tail latency for a product that affects clinical notes ingestion.

[02:05] Lena: Data pipelines are near-real-time, about 30-60s latency for the metrics we show. Traces are sampled but you can turn on full tracing for specific routes for a short window. For alerts you can plug our webhook or send to Datadog.

[10:15] Lena: Jumping into per-route dashboards now. Here's Route: /notes-summarize. You can see token breakdown per model version, cost per 1k tokens, and expected monthly spend given current traffic. We also show the batching efficiency and effective tokens per GPU-second. You can annotate routes, set a priority (latency-first vs cost-first), and the smart router will route accordingly—hosted on our fastest pools or fall back to cheaper variants.

[18:30] Samir: To map that to your question earlier—if you pin /notes-summarize to Dedicated capacity you get predictable throughput and lower tail latency, but you pay for reserved capacity. For bursty or lower-priority routes, routing to hosted or quantized variants can save a lot. Example: for long-context summarization we often recommend mixed approach—Dedicated for interactive API, Hosted or quantized variant for batch jobs.

[27:00] Maya: We have a lot of PII in notes; are we able to keep data on-prem or in our VPC? How does key management work?

[27:45] Samir: Good question. For Solaris Health we'd look at Redwood Private—this gives you a customer-managed control plane and you can deploy in VPC or on-prem. We integrate with KMS/HSM for envelope encryption and you get audit logs and RBAC. Lena, feel free to call out the logs location.

[28:10] Lena: Audit logs are exported to your S3 or GCS bucket, and we also stream syslogs if you want SIEM integration. For KMS we support AWS KMS and commonly used HSM providers. Note: some field names in older docs show service as "Redwood Consul"—that's just a transcription mismatch in our docs.

[34:45] Alex: On cost breakdown, show me the lever example. If we increase batching, what's the tradeoff in latency? And do we get estimated savings in the console?

[35:10] Lena: Yes — in the route view there's a simulator. You can toggle batching window from 0ms to 50ms, choose quantization profile (int8, int4) and see projected cost delta and expected 95th latency. For your /notes-summarize route with average 2k tokens, we estimate 18-25% cost reduction with a 20ms batch window and int8 quant, with 10-15% tail latency increase in some worst-case patterns. We also surface quality delta from our regressions if you attach eval sets.

[36:05] Priya: On compliance—SOC2 and ISO—do you have those artifacts? Also data residency for EU customers?

[36:30] Samir: We do. We'll share SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. For EU residency we can pin routing to EU regions and for Private installs we can run in your cloud region. We'll also include details on data retention and deletion APIs.

[40:00] Maya: This is helpful. For the POC we'd like Redwood to run a benchmark using our sample traffic and the same model weights we plan to use. Can you mirror our traffic patterns?

[40:20] Samir: Yes, we can run a POC bench. Action items: Alex will send top 10 routes and a sample traffic CSV, Lena will propose batching/quant config and a quantization profile, Samir will send pricing and Dedicated options, and Priya will send any compliance Qs. We'll aim to kick off the POC next week.

[42:10] Alex: One small nit—what about fallbacks if Dedicated capacity is saturated? We can't have production downtime.

[42:30] Lena: We support overflow routing: canary to hosted or lower-tier quantized variants, and automatic throttles. You can set SLOs and a fallback policy per route.

[44:00] Samir: Great. Quick recap of next steps and timelines, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark run and attach the SOC2, pricing, and the console recording. Any last questions?

[44:20] Maya: None from me. Thanks, this was clear.

[44:30] Priya: Thanks everyone.

[44:40] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
